Create an isolated, sparse winter settlement in a broad snow-filled basin enclosed by wooded hills. Set it at warm, hazy sunset, with deep ivory snowdrifts, long blue-gray shadows, and occasional falling snow. Leave the central landscape largely undeveloped, using rolling wind-sculpted snowbanks, shallow gullies, exposed patches of dark road or water, scattered shrubs, and a few small frozen pools or irregular black openings in the ice.

Place the main residential cluster along one side of a frozen lake or broad flooded plain. Arrange roughly three large, tall slab-shaped apartment blocks, each about ten stories, loosely around short access roads and open courtyards rather than packed into a continuous street wall. Use repetitive grid façades of weathered beige concrete, small rectangular windows in rows, and darker recessed balcony bands. In front of and between these towers, scatter about five smaller boxy brick apartment buildings, generally four or five stories high. Give them snow-covered hipped or flat roofs, chimneys, antennas, and a few warmly lit windows.

Take a narrow cracked asphalt road past the buildings and around the courtyards, then along the lake. Continue it over the frozen water on a long, straight, low bridge with simple supporting piers. Line parts of the lakeside road and open ground with segmented decorative concrete fencing.

Among the snowy slopes and woods, distribute several isolated cottages or utility-like brick structures, including a weathered two-story masonry house with a chimney, rooftop antennas, and rising smoke. Arrange vegetation organically: dense stands of snow-laden birch and pine near the settlement, sparser leafless trees and twisted bushes across open mounds, and thicker evergreen forests climbing the surrounding hills. Let uneven snowy ridges, forested mountains, and the frozen lake form a dissolving outer boundary. Keep the whole composition quiet, spacious, weathered, and only lightly inhabited.
